_comment_feedback_encoding: CANONICAL DRIVER-FEEDBACK ENCODING (project-lead + reviewer decision, 2026-07-27): signed-bipolar per the recorded scale definition (ui/views/outing_form.py's feedback-table caption) -- negative=understeer, positive=oversteer, magnitude bands roughly |2..3|='clearly felt', |4..5|='approaching undrivable'/'undrivable'. Every condition.verdict <-> condition.feedback_sign pairing in this file must agree with this map (modules/recommendation.py's VERDICT_EXPECTED_FEEDBACK_SIGN: understeer->negative, oversteer->positive; unstable_yaw has no feedback-sign axis at all). Verified 2026-07-27 against every rule below (26 non-retired + 7 retired seeds): all already agree, none needed changing. The consistency-gate feedback_override (settings.consistency_gate.feedback_override below) also keys off this same map -- repaired the same day, since it previously checked feedback MAGNITUDE only and could have been overridden by a complaint in the wrong direction.
_comment_parameters: suggestion.parameter values are config/setup_parameters.json registry keys (WP2b-1). A rule's suggestion is either a single action object or a list of action objects (an atomic package -- e.g. wing+rake -- or an axle-symmetric FL+FR/RL+RR pair, since the registry has no combined axle-level ARB/camber/damper key, see arb_fl notes). Every action is either delta-style {parameter, direction, delta} (delta is SIGNED, in the parameter's native unit/step -- feasibility is current_value + delta against the registry's value_space min/max) or target-style {parameter, target} (a literal value, used only for categorical parameters like abs_position where 'direction' has no meaning -- always feasible, never checked against setup_data). weight moved from suggestion to the rule's own top level in WP2b-2 (a scoring parameter, not a physical-action parameter, and suggestion can now be a list).
_comment_trigger: condition.trigger selects how a rule fires. 'data': fires from classify_fn (verdict + min_severity) on the rule's phases; feedback_sign/min_feedback_abs only modulate the score (agreement_bonus / conflict_penalty / 1.0 if feedback absent). 'driver': fires from feedback_sign/min_feedback_abs on the rule's phases alone (score scales with max |feedback|/5 among those phases); condition.verdict is NOT a firing gate here -- it is only the agreement reference against which classify_fn's verdict on the same phases is compared, to modulate the score (agreement_bonus if it matches, conflict_penalty + the corner listed in conflicts if it contradicts with the opposite axle verdict, 1.0 if data is silent/ok). 'both': fires only when the data condition AND the driver condition both hold independently -- no further modulation, higher default weight (high-confidence tier).
_comment_source_balance: settings.source_balance (0..1) is a global multiplier on top of the per-trigger score, applied after agreement/conflict modulation: data-triggered rules get (1 - source_balance) * 2, driver-triggered rules get source_balance * 2, both-triggered rules always get 1.0 (corroborated evidence is never discounted). Default 0.5 is exactly neutral (both multipliers = 1.0, current behaviour unchanged). At the extremes a single-source rule still fires and evaluates -- its match, corner, and conflict flag still exist -- but its score multiplies to 0 and it drops out at min_score_to_show, which is suppression at the scoring stage only, not at the evaluation stage. source_balance does not touch agreement_bonus/conflict_penalty: balance weighs WHO may raise a hypothesis, modulation weighs WHAT the other source says about it.
_comment_worst_corner: settings.worst_corner_multiplier scales EVERY match's score on a corner the driver flagged as 'worst' in the feedback table, regardless of trigger type -- applied once, after source_balance and agreement/conflict modulation. It is orthogonal to both: source_balance weighs who may raise a hypothesis, agreement/conflict weighs what the other source says about a specific match, worst_corner_multiplier weighs the driver's own prioritisation of which corner matters most this outing. Default 1.5; a corner with no 'worst' flag is unaffected (implicit x1.0). Multiple flagged corners each get the multiplier independently.
_comment_cell_id_status: cell_id is the forward-reference key into the engineer decision matrix (external, maintained outside this repo) that a matrix-derived rule encodes -- document leads code, every matrix cell has exactly one JSON entry, including the two cells the matrix defines no action for (OS-BRK-low, INST-ENT) and the escalation cells not yet activated. status extends seed|reviewed to: elicited (matrix-derived, sourced from the authoritative decision matrix but not yet engineering-reviewed in-tool -- NOT a placeholder guess the way the old ARB-only seeds were), held (escalation rule, fully specified for 1:1 traceability but never fires -- no applied-recommendations history exists yet to know whether the base change was tried, see each held rule's rationale), dropped (matrix cell deliberately defines no action -- recorded, never fires), retired (superseded, kept for history, never fires). generate_recommendations skips any rule whose status is held, dropped, or retired.
_comment_severity_floor_repair: Repair (2026-07-27): the four held escalation rules under a CS-only verdict (understeer) -- US-BRK-low-esc, US-BRK-med-esc, US-BRK-high-esc, US-APX-med-esc -- previously carried min_severity='strong', which is structurally unreachable from their own single-phase evaluation: _classify_corner's severity='strong' branch requires BOTH strong-CS AND destabilising yaw on the SAME restricted phase slice these rules evaluate (their own phases list, e.g. just entry_1_brake), but these rules exist to escalate a WORSENING CS-only understeer reading, which has nothing to do with yaw instability. Left as 'strong', none of the four could ever fire even after promotion out of 'held' status (a future WP) -- corrected to min_severity='moderate' so the advisory/recommended split and provenance caps (settings.action_class), not an accidentally-unreachable severity gate, are what govern proportionality, which is their actual job.
_comment_consistency_gate: Global policy (decision matrix): no recommendation unless the triggering verdict repeats across laps for the same stable_corner_id. Evaluated per-lap (not just on the median-of-medians aggregate) for every 'data'/'both'-trigger rule: min_repeat_laps is an absolute floor, min_repeat_fraction is a fraction of that corner's analysed laps -- BOTH must hold (AND, not OR). 'driver'-trigger rules are exempt (driver feedback has no lap dimension, see _feedback_row).
_comment_consistency_gate_feedback_overr: Feedback override (project-lead-elicited 2026-07-27, engineer-validation line added to PLAN.md; full rationale + scale semantics also in thesis_notes.md): a candidate passes the consistency gate with an effective min_repeat_laps of 1 (bypassing BOTH the normal min_repeat_laps AND min_repeat_fraction checks, not just the laps floor -- with only 1 of typically 4 laps required, the 0.4 fraction default would otherwise still reject it) when BOTH raw |feedback| >= feedback_override_raw_min AND scaled |feedback| >= feedback_override_scaled_min (scaled = raw * the driver_level_weighting multiplier, PART A). Two separate floors, not one, deliberately: the raw floor (4) keys off the elicited driver feedback-scale semantics -- +-2..3 is 'clearly felt', +-4..5 is 'approaching undrivable' -- so raw>=4 means the driver is reporting the car is nearly undrivable at that phase, not merely noticeable; the scaled floor (4.0, coincidentally the same number as the raw floor but a distinct, independently-configured value) exists specifically to stop a LOW driving_level's inflated-relative-to-skill raw complaint from piercing the gate on weight alone -- a raw-4 complaint from a level-1 driver (weight 0.6) scales to 2.4, well under 4.0, and is correctly refused the override; only a driver whose feedback is both objectively in the undrivable region AND whose level-weighted magnitude also clears the same bar gets the single-lap pass. Rationale: a strong, unprompted driver complaint on a corner already showing a moderate+ data verdict is itself consistency evidence -- a capable driver will not provoke the same imbalance repeatedly (across laps) just to make the data repeat, so demanding multi-lap repetition on top of a near-undrivable complaint is asking the data to double-confirm what the driver already has. See modules/recommendation.py _consistency_gate_ok.
_comment_escalation_enabled: Undrivable-feedback tier (design ruling, project-lead-elicited 2026-07-28; repaired 2026-07-28 turn 2 to match against LAP-LEVEL verdict instances, not the median-of-medians aggregate -- see thesis_notes.md 'Undrivable tier: lap-level cell matching'): 'escalation_enabled' reuses this SAME feedback_override block's raw_min/scaled_min pair (deliberately not a third, separately-tunable threshold -- |4| is one elicited undrivable boundary, not two) to drive a stronger, structural guarantee than the consistency-gate override above: at |raw feedback| >= feedback_override_raw_min the tool must never render silent emptiness for that corner, honesty via labeling rather than suppression. See modules/recommendation.py _apply_undrivable_escalation for the three exhaustive outcomes: pierce/synthesize every soft cap (forced to recommended, tagged URGENT with a rationale line naming the real per-lap pattern) when some non-retired rule shows lap-level evidence -- severity at or above that rule's own min_severity on at least one analysed lap, checked across every phase/rule the feedback's implied direction could cover, not just the phase the driver happened to rate worst -- and the scaled floor also clears (if the rule never produced a match against the aggregate, it is re-run through the normal rule/bucket path with the qualifying lap's own data substituted in, so the resulting row carries a real suggestion, not a placeholder); a synthetic 'no elicited rule covers this case' row when no rule shows lap-level evidence in either direction anywhere for the corner; an urgent contradiction row, carrying the existing conflict badge, when some rule's lap-level evidence is the OPPOSITE axle direction from what the feedback implies. The turn-2 repair was needed because the original aggregate-only check could report a spurious gap for a corner whose real per-lap pattern (e.g. moderate understeer on 2 of 4 laps) diluted to 'normal' in the aggregate, or lived at a different phase than the one the feedback named. Rationale for the scale's own top band, carried exactly as elicited: |5| is the driver reporting they are milliseconds from crashing -- a report at that magnitude must always reach the engineer, never wash out under a provenance cap, a situational rule's permanent-advisory status, or a low aggregate score. Set false to disable the whole tier and fall back to pre-2026-07-28 behaviour (the consistency-gate override above is unaffected either way).
_comment_change_budget: Distinct from max_recommendations (a DISPLAY cap, unchanged -- up to 8 ranked results still render for context). change_budget governs which results get the 'selected' marker: the tool marks the top default_max non-conflicted, feasible results as selected after ranking (severity, corner count, escalation_tier, cell_id -- see modules/recommendation.py ranking), walking further down the ranked list to fill the budget if a higher-ranked result is parameter_conflict or infeasible. absolute_cap is exposed for a future manual engineer override UI; the tool itself never auto-selects past default_max.
_comment_action_class: WP2b-2 amendment 7: a 'data'-trigger match at moderate severity with no driver corroboration on the same phases is ADVISORY (an observation + most likely lever, non-imperative rationale, never budget-eligible) rather than RECOMMENDED -- mild understeer is this car's deliberate stable baseline (June driver-report precedent) and the elicitation's own bias is against unnecessary changes when the driver is inconsistent with the data. A match is RECOMMENDED if its trigger is in always_recommended_triggers (driver/both are already corroborated by construction), or if trigger is 'data' and either severity is in data_trigger_recommended_severities (default: 'strong') or driver feedback on the same phases agrees with the data verdict (corroborated). A bucket is RECOMMENDED if ANY of its matches reach that bar, else ADVISORY -- advisory-only matches still contribute evidence/score, they just cannot carry the bucket to budget-eligible on their own.
_comment_driver_level_weighting: PART A (2026-07-27): Driver.driving_level (models/driver.py, Integer 1-10, DriverDialog's own '1 = lowest, 10 = highest' hint) resolves to a feedback_weight multiplier applied ONCE where fb_value is computed (modules/recommendation.py _evaluate_rule) -- before any trigger branch reads it. This scales the 'driver'-trigger score contribution directly (weight * |fb|/5 * factor * driver_source_factor) AND the 'data'/'both'-trigger corroboration criterion (_feedback_modulation's min_feedback_abs/sign check runs against the WEIGHTED value, so a higher-level driver's complaint clears the corroboration bar -- the one that lifts a moderate data-trigger match to RECOMMENDED -- more readily than the same raw feedback from a lower-level driver). neutral_level=5 keeps a driver with no strong level opinion assigned at exactly today's unweighted behaviour; default_weight covers driving_level=None or an out-of-table value. Stated consequence, not hidden: because this scales fb_value before a 'driver'-trigger rule's own firing gate (abs(fb_value) < min_feedback_abs), a low-level driver's borderline feedback can fail to fire a driver-trigger rule at all, not just score lower -- an intended effect of weighting driver-sourced contributions, not a bug. Table values are elicited content (project-lead-elicited 2026-07-27, not derived from data) -- see PLAN.md engineer follow-up list for the validation line.

rules.name: Entry understeer (data) -> soften front ARB
rules.rationale: Softens the front ARB to reduce front lateral load transfer and free up grip on the sliding front axle at turn-in.

rules.name: Exit oversteer / traction (data) -> soften rear ARB
rules.rationale: Softens the rear ARB to reduce rear lateral load transfer and restore traction and stability under power on exit.

rules.name: Apex understeer (data) -> soften front ARB
rules.rationale: Softens the front ARB to reduce front lateral load transfer and free up front grip through a sustained, high-load apex.

rules.name: Unstable yaw on entry (data) -> soften rear ARB
rules.rationale: Softens the rear ARB to free up rear grip and add yaw damping while trail-braking into the corner.

rules.name: Driver-reported exit oversteer (driver) -> soften rear ARB
rules.rationale: Softens the rear ARB to free up rear grip and address the driver's reported exit oversteer.

rules.name: Driver-reported entry understeer (driver) -> soften front ARB
rules.rationale: Softens the front ARB to free up front grip and address the driver's reported entry understeer.

rules.name: Entry understeer, data + driver agree (both) -> soften front ARB
rules.rationale: Data and driver agree on entry understeer: softening the front ARB frees up front grip at turn-in.

rules.name: Understeer, braking, low speed -> ABS front-stable map
rules.rationale: Add 0.5mm front toe-out to sharpen turn-in response and address front-axle understeer risk under braking at low speed. If that isn't enough, an ABS map change is the next lever (see the escalation note).

rules.name: Escalation: US-BRK-low -> ABS try-and-error, FA stability target
rules.rationale: If front toe-out alone doesn't resolve it, try 1-2 ABS positions toward the front-axle-stable map within the current dry grip bracket.

rules.name: Understeer, braking, medium speed -> front bump LS softer
rules.rationale: Open front low-speed bump damping 3 clicks (both corners) to soften nose-dive control and slow front-axle load transfer under trail-braking.

rules.name: Escalation: US-BRK-med -> front ARB softer, rear ARB stiffer
rules.rationale: If the damper change alone isn't enough, soften front ARB 2 positions and stiffen rear ARB 1 position to shift roll stiffness rearward and free up front-axle grip under trail-braking.

rules.name: Understeer, braking, high speed -> wing up + rake forward (package)
rules.rationale: One wing step up plus 1mm of forward rake (front ride height down, rear up) adds rear downforce and shifts the aero balance rearward, raising braking-phase stability so more front grip stays available. Applied together as one package.

rules.name: Escalation: US-BRK-high -> front bump HS softer
rules.rationale: If the wing+rake package alone doesn't resolve it, open front high-speed bump damping 2 clicks for extra compliance.

rules.name: Understeer, turn-in, low speed -> front toe more toe-out
rules.rationale: Add 0.5mm front toe-out to sharpen initial turn-in response and counter front-axle understeer at low speed.

rules.name: Understeer, turn-in, medium speed -> diff position down
rules.rationale: Drop the differential one locking-torque position to let the front axle rotate more freely into the corner on turn-in trail-throttle.

rules.name: Understeer, turn-in, high speed -> wing down
rules.rationale: Drop the wing one step to reduce rear downforce and shift the aero balance toward more front grip at turn-in speed.

rules.name: Understeer, apex, low speed -> front ARB softer
rules.rationale: Soften the front ARB 1 position (both corners) to free up mid-corner front grip under sustained apex load. Alternative: stiffen the rear ARB 1 position instead, which rotates the car more and eases the same understeer.

rules.name: Understeer, apex, medium speed -> diff position down
rules.rationale: Drop the differential one locking-torque position to ease the understeer a locked diff can induce through the apex under partial throttle.

rules.name: Escalation: US-APX-med -> TC LAT up (power-understeer)
rules.rationale: If the diff change alone isn't enough, raise TC LAT one position -- cuts torque sooner under lateral load, keeping more reserve on the front axle. Only applies when throttle is involved (on-power understeer), not an off-throttle push.

rules.name: Understeer, apex, high speed -> front camber more negative
rules.rationale: Add 0.1deg more front negative camber (both corners) to add peak front grip under sustained high-speed apex load. Typical practice is a 0.2deg step (two clicks); check tyre wear pattern first, and consider a one-sided change if only one corner needs it.

rules.name: Understeer, exit, low speed -> TC LON down
rules.rationale: Drop TC LON one position to allow a touch more wheel spin, easing power-on understeer at low exit speed.

rules.name: Understeer, exit, medium speed -> rear ARB stiffer
rules.rationale: Stiffen the rear ARB 1 position (both corners) to rotate the car more on exit and counter the understeer.

rules.name: Understeer, exit, high speed -> rear ARB stiffer
rules.rationale: Same fix as medium-speed exit understeer: stiffen the rear ARB 1 position (both corners) to rotate the car more on exit.

rules.name: Oversteer, braking, low speed -> none
rules.rationale: No first-change action defined for this scenario; recorded for completeness, never fires.

rules.name: Oversteer, braking, medium speed -> rear ARB softer
rules.rationale: Soften the rear ARB 1 position to free up rear grip under brake-release yaw.

rules.name: Oversteer, braking, high speed -> rear ARB softer
rules.rationale: Same fix as medium-speed braking oversteer: soften the rear ARB 1 position to free up rear grip.

rules.name: Oversteer, turn-in, low speed -> front toe toward zero
rules.rationale: Reduce front toe-out by 0.5mm toward zero to calm the extra turn-in rotation toe-out adds, easing oversteer at low speed.

rules.name: Oversteer, turn-in, medium speed -> diff position up
rules.rationale: Add one differential locking-torque position to stabilise the rear axle on turn-in trail-throttle.

rules.name: Oversteer, turn-in, high speed -> wing up
rules.rationale: Add one wing step to add rear downforce and counter rear instability at turn-in speed.

rules.name: Oversteer, apex, low speed -> front ARB stiffer
rules.rationale: Under sustained apex load, two valid levers depending on which axle is closer to its limit: stiffen front ARB 1 position, or soften rear ARB 1 position instead. Engineer's call, not a fixed first change.

rules.name: Oversteer, apex, medium speed -> diff position up
rules.rationale: Under partial throttle, add one diff locking-torque position to stabilise the rear axle, or address it through toe/camber/ARB instead -- engineer's call.

rules.name: Oversteer, apex, high speed -> front camber less negative
rules.rationale: Under sustained high-speed apex load, three possible levers: a spring change, softening rear ARB 1 position, or 0.1deg less front negative camber -- engineer's call on which fits the car at the time.

rules.name: Oversteer, exit, low speed -> TC LON up
rules.rationale: Add one TC LON position to cut wheel spin and reduce power-on rear-axle oversteer.

rules.name: Oversteer, exit, medium speed -> rear ARB softer
rules.rationale: Soften the rear ARB 1 position to free up rear grip on power application.

rules.name: Oversteer, exit, high speed -> wing up
rules.rationale: Add one wing step to add rear downforce and stability on power application at high exit speed.

rules.name: Instability, braking, low speed -> ABS rear-stable map
rules.rationale: Try 1-2 ABS positions toward the rear-axle-stable map within the current dry grip bracket, to calm unstable yaw under braking at low speed.

rules.name: Instability, braking, medium speed -> rake reduction
rules.rationale: Reduce rake by 1mm (front ride height up, rear down) to shift the aero pressure centre forward and calm destabilising yaw while trail-braking.

rules.name: Instability, braking, high speed -> front toe more toe-out
rules.rationale: Add 0.5mm front toe-out to sharpen the front axle's response to counter-steer input, adding authority against destabilising yaw while trail-braking.

rules.name: Instability, combined entry -> dropped
rules.rationale: No first-change action defined for combined entry instability; recorded for completeness, never fires.

_comment_elicitation_provenance: Provenance of each matrix-derived/held rule against the external decision matrix record, applied 2026-07-26 from the authoritative markup supplied for this ruleset: engineer-verbatim (12 elicited cells + 2 held escalations that inherit it -- a first-change lever the engineer stated directly, unmarked in the matrix), project-default (8 elicited cells, asterisked in the matrix -- a default this project chose absent a clean explicit engineer statement for that exact cell: US-BRK-low/garbled ABS answer, US-TIN-high/wing direction, US-APX-low/bare "ARB" defaulted to front, US-APX-high/camber step, OS-BRK-high/bare "rear ARB" presumed -1, OS-EXIT-med/sign-corrected from the engineer's stated "+1" (the S8-Med case), INST-BRK-low/ABS defaulted, INST-BRK-high/axle presumed front -- plus 1 held escalation, US-BRK-high-esc, whose bump-HS direction was also defaulted, not inherited from its verbatim base cell US-BRK-high), mirror-derived (6 cells marked "m" in the matrix -- OS-TIN-low/med/high, OS-APX-low/med/high -- structurally mirrored from the opposite-verdict cell's lever, not independently stated for this cell). null for dropped/retired rules (never fire, provenance moot). Policy (settings.action_class.cap_non_verbatim_to_advisory): a rule whose provenance is not engineer-verbatim is capped to ADVISORY regardless of severity/corroboration, UNTIL an engineer confirms that specific cell and its status is promoted to "reviewed" -- the cap is config-resident (can be switched off globally) but the INTENDED lift path is per-cell via status, not the global switch. Confirmation list for the engineer: exactly the 8 project-default + 6 mirror-derived cells (see PLAN.md engineer follow-up questions).
